{{Short description|Circles whose tangent lines at the points of intersection are perpendicular}}
{{inline |date=May 2024}}
[[File:Orthogonal circles.svg|thumb|Three mutually orthogonal circles]]

In [[geometry]], two [[circle]]s are said to be '''orthogonal''' if their respective [[tangent lines to circles|tangent line]]s at the points of [[intersection (geometry)|intersection]] are [[perpendicular]] (meet at a [[right angle]]).

A straight line through a circle's center is orthogonal to it. Straight lines may also considered as a kind of [[generalized circle]]s, for instance in [[inversive geometry]]. An orthogonal pair of lines or line and circle are orthogonal generalized circles. Straight lines are the only generalized circles that pass through the center of a circle to which they are orthogonal.

In the [[Poincaré disk model|conformal disk model]] of the [[hyperbolic plane]], every [[geodesic]] is an arc of a generalized circle orthogonal to the circle of [[ideal point]]s bounding the disk.
